skill.summary: Builds Bauplan pipeline projects with branch-safe workflows, SQL source nodes, Python transformations, materialized outputs, and data quality checks.

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from markdown backticks, Python import examples, table samples, and assertion text. I found one contextual medium risk: user-provided branch and table identifiers are inserted into Bauplan CLI and SQL preview commands without validation guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Validate branch, namespace, and table identifiers against expected patterns before running Bauplan commands. Quote shell arguments where the tool supports it.
Require explicit user confirmation before bauplan run. Document that REPLACE and APPEND can change lakehouse tables.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated CLI Arguments in Workflow Templates
semantic_findings.description: The workflow asks assistants to place branch, namespace, and table names directly into Bauplan CLI and SQL preview commands. Malformed identifiers could alter shell or SQL behavior if an assistant copies them without validation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file clearly templates user-controlled branch and table identifiers into shell and SQL commands. The skill does not include explicit identifier validation or shell quoting guidance.

content.value_statement: Bauplan projects need clear DAG structure, branch safety, and consistent SQL or Python model patterns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through pipeline files, validation, and safe run workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates Bauplan project structure with a project configuration and model files.
Guides SQL first-node models that read from existing lakehouse tables.
Guides Python transformation models with Bauplan decorators and pinned package versions.
Supports materialization choices for final outputs, including REPLACE and APPEND.
Adds data quality expectations and output column validation patterns.
Provides dry-run and strict-mode workflow steps for pipeline checks.
limitations: Requires the Bauplan CLI and user credentials to be configured outside the skill.
Assumes source tables already exist in the Bauplan lakehouse.
Does not validate live schemas unless the assistant runs approved Bauplan CLI commands.
Generated transformations still need review against business rules and data contracts.

use_cases.title: Start a New Analytics Pipeline
use_cases.description: Create a Bauplan project with source nodes, transformations, materialized outputs, and a dry-run workflow.

use_cases.title: Convert Business Logic into Models
use_cases.description: Turn transformation requirements into SQL source models and Python downstream models with clear DAG dependencies.

use_cases.title: Add Data Quality Checks
use_cases.description: Define expectations, output schemas, and strict-mode checks before publishing pipeline results.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one source table and one output table.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Bauplan pipeline for [goal] using source table [table]. Ask me for missing branch, output, and materialization details before writing files.

prompt_templates.title: Add Python Transformations
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow with downstream Python models.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Bauplan DAG for [business logic]. Use SQL only for first source reads, then use Python models with declared output columns.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Input Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-input Bauplan model that joins [table A] and [table B]. Use I/O pushdown, docstrings, and materialized final outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Harden and Validate a Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before running a pipeline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Bauplan pipeline for branch safety, materialization choices, strict mode, expectations, and schema validation. Suggest fixes before any run.

output_examples.input: Create a taxi trip pipeline with zone enrichment and a daily summary output.
output: A Bauplan project plan with source tables, DAG order, and final materialized outputs.
A SQL first node for lakehouse reads and Python models for enrichment and summary logic.
A dry-run checklist that verifies branch, source tables, and materialization settings.

output_examples.input: Add quality checks for order identifiers and trip distance values.
output: Expectation functions for non-null identifiers, unique identifiers, and reasonable distance values.
Guidance for strict-mode runs so expectation failures stop the pipeline early.

output_examples.input: Review my Bauplan model plan before I run it.
output: A review of SQL versus Python model placement, output columns, and I/O pushdown usage.
A list of required confirmations before running state-changing Bauplan commands.

best_practices: Use a development branch and run a dry run before any full pipeline run.
Declare output columns and use I/O pushdown for every model when possible.
Confirm materialization strategy for each final table before running the pipeline.
anti_patterns: Running pipeline commands on the main branch.
Using SQL models for downstream transformations after the first lakehouse read.
Leaving branch names, table names, or SQL preview queries unchecked before execution.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates Bauplan pipeline project guidance, including configuration, SQL models, Python models, expectations, and run checklists.

faq.question: Does it run pipelines automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide approved Bauplan CLI use, but users should confirm state-changing runs before execution.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code in environments that can access the project files and allowed tools.

faq.question: Can it write both SQL and Python models?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses SQL for first source reads and Python for downstream transformations.

faq.question: Does it require existing source tables?
faq.answer: Yes. Source tables must already exist in the Bauplan lakehouse before the pipeline can run.

faq.question: How does it handle data quality?
faq.answer: It can add Bauplan expectations, declared output columns, docstrings, and strict-mode checks for early validation.
